claims.value: Bodart: side A (French) 16,000 covering army under Saint-Cyr then Augereau and 18,000 besiegers under Verdier, total 34,000; side B (Spanish) garrison increased through reinforcements to 9,400; not an opening strength.
claims.rationale: Claim-relevant rendering of the contextual quote/table. Bodart’s rounded-up available-for-engagement convention is shared, not an opening muster. Source-specific component/time distinctions remain. English rendering (ours): "Side A: 16,000 covering army under Saint-Cyr then Augereau and 18,000 besiegers under Verdier, total 34,000. Side B: garrison increased through reinforcements to 9,400; not an opening strength."

claims.value: Toreno gives side B 5,673 of all arms at the opening of the third siege, separate from the civilian population.
claims.rationale: Opening garrison, not Bodart’s reinforced peak or capitulation survivors. English rendering (ours): "At the beginning of the third siege its garrison numbered 5,673 of all arms."

claims.value: Saint-Cyr says the incomplete Spanish garrison did not reach 3,000 before commencement; this conflicts in population/time with Toreno’s opening 5,673.
claims.rationale: French opponent estimate in the pre-siege preparations, not a matching own return. No averaging. English rendering (ours): "Gerona’s garrison was far from complete; it did not reach three thousand men."

citations.locator: saint-cyr, printed p. 161, Internet Archive leaf 165; inspected page-image excerpt

claims.value: Saint-Cyr gives side A 18,000 under Verdier after Lechi’s reinforcement on 22 May and approximately 12,000 combatants in the reduced observation corps.
claims.rationale: Dated preparation allocations, not all simultaneous besiegers or Bodart’s later covering population. No implied stable siege-long total. English rendering (ours): "This brought Verdier’s troops to eighteen thousand and reduced the observation corps to twenty-one battalions, about twelve thousand combatants."

citations.locator: saint-cyr, printed p. 163, Internet Archive leaf 167; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: ce qui porta à dix-huit mille hommes le nombre des troupes sous les ordres du général Verdier, et réduisit le corps d’observation à vingt-un bataillons, formant environ douze mille combattants.

claims.value: Saint-Cyr describes Lechi’s reinforcement placed at Verdier’s disposal, while the chief retained the observation corps; later Augereau arrived before the place on 11 or 12 October.
claims.rationale: October from surrounding chronology. Appointment, arrival and effective replacement are not collapsed into one proven boundary. Cover/siege commands remain separate. English rendering (ours): "On 22 May he placed Lechi with seven battalions and two squadrons at his disposal; [Augereau] arrived before the place on the 11th or 12th."

claims.value: Toreno says Alvarez continued giving orders until 8 December and relinquished command to Julian Bolivar on the 9th during a lucid interval.
claims.rationale: Late-siege authority change as narrated, not a verified exact timestamp or admitted tactical replacement boundary. English rendering (ours): "He continued issuing orders until the 8th; after delirium, on the 9th in a lucid interval he relinquished command to the lieutenant governor Julian Bolivar."

claims.value: Toreno gives side B 1,100 effective men on 8 December, distinct from all remaining garrison/prisoner populations.
claims.rationale: Late-siege effective subset; not opening strength or all survivors. English rendering (ours): "Eleven hundred men were the effective force."

claims.value: Saint-Cyr describes continuing the French blockade under Augereau.
claims.rationale: Inherited investment at his arrival; does not convert Spanish relief operations into a second siege victory. English rendering (ours): "Augereau on arriving in Catalonia found no obstacle to continuing the blockade of Gerona."

claims.value: Toreno describes negotiated capitulation with Augereau and French entry on 11 December; entry is separate from Bodart’s 10 December capitulation endpoint.
claims.rationale: No different victor claimed; surrender and subsequent occupation clocks distinguished. English rendering (ours): "The French entered the place on 11 December by the Areny gate."

claims.value: Toreno describes the city extending onto both banks of the Oña.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "It later extended along both banks of the Oña."

claims.value: Saint-Cyr attributes the city’s final condition partly to lack of subsistence, fatigue and disease.
claims.rationale: Retrospective attribution at the siege endpoint, not an opening readiness measure or causal estimate. English rendering (ours): "Deprived of part of its population and garrison by lack of subsistence, fatigue and disease."

claims.value: Toreno says the councils received notice that relief would not arrive with the desired promptness before negotiating capitulation.
claims.rationale: Late-siege communicated expectation, not a verified independent forecast. English rendering (ours): "Having received notice from the Catalan congress that its relief would not arrive with the desired promptness."
